description: Field names and values forbidden on current Arkret v1 wire only in the registered context. Consumers MUST first select context_definitions using the trusted document kind and owning schema reference, then apply the entry matcher inside the selected instance_pointer and match_scope. A same-named field in another context is not forbidden by this entry. allowed_contexts only exempts references in documentation, interop definitions and negative tests; it never exempts submitted wire data.

rejection_levels.hard_reject: Reducer / parser MUST fail with schema_violation when the field appears in the listed context.

allowed_context_definitions.interop_module: Reference in an explicit interop binding (e.g., MIMI interop) where the cross-protocol mapping requires the field.
allowed_context_definitions.negative_test: Reference in negative fixtures / cotest drift tests that assert rejection.

context_matching.selection: Selectors are alternatives. wire matches all wire documents, including schema_instance. schema_instance matches an exact owning schema_ref (filename plus optional JSON Pointer fragment, normalized without ./). Event payload schema_ref is resolved from event-kind-registry.json, never guessed from field names. Nested typed instances retain their own schema_ref. A consumer MUST supply the semantic document kind from its validated owning contract, never from untrusted payload claims. A definition with status=closed has no selectors and MUST NOT be selected by any active wire caller; it is an explicit empty domain, not an unspecified catch-all.
context_matching.instance_pointer: RFC 6901 tokens relative to the typed instance root; * selects each immediate object member or array element. Empty string selects the instance itself. Missing pointer selects nothing. root compares fields/paths relative to the selected root only; descendants repeats that comparison at every descendant object. Neither mode searches inside encoded ciphertext or free-text string content. patch applies the selected create-context field/path matcher to the canonical patch object at that root: exact/descendant paths and ancestor replacement values are checked. This explicit transform preserves the create domain without inventing a context mapping in consumers.
context_matching.entry_matching: id remains an audit identifier. match.kind selects field (literal member name), path (dot-separated member path relative to root), patch_path (property names of the canonical patch object defined by patch.schema.json), value (exact scalar value), prefix (scalar prefix), or pattern (scalar regular expression). match.values are alternatives. No heuristic interpretation of id is permitted. patch_path rejects its exact path and descendants for every operation. For an ancestor set/add or direct-value replacement, inspect the replacement value at the remaining registered path. A patch is never an array of path/op records. Patch value objects MUST also be checked against their owning create payload contexts; replacing an ancestor does not bypass a nested forbidden path.

Encrypted Envelope MUST NOT carry `cleartext_commitment`. The bare plaintext hash is dictionary-attackable offline against low-entropy plaintext; v1 E2EE producers MUST NOT emit it and receivers MUST reject any envelope that carries it (top-level `not.required` in schemas/encrypted-envelope.schema.json). Future profiles needing plaintext commitment MUST define a keyed/salted form rather than this bare hash.

Both cowrite_policy and co_write_policy are forbidden. Which typed current result families an Event kind writes — and which writes form an atomic unit — is fixed by the contract-registry result_writes contracts and registered atomic units. v1 defines no Realm-configurable co-write whitelist. Any future per-Realm co-write constraint requires complete governance-Station admission and domain-transition rules and cannot appear as a bare optional field.

The Event carries no producer-side revision counter. Ordering is assigned by the accepting governance Station as the RealmCommit stream_position; a producer-declared revision would let the signer claim an order it cannot hold.

The Event carries no hybrid logical clock. A producer clock is not protocol order. 'hlc' remains legal in Station-local projections such as read-cursor position and Agent sidecar view state, which are not Events.
The Event carries no separate domain reference array. Registered business references travel in 'refs'; authorization dependencies are resolved inside the admission transaction.

The Event carries no precondition array. Concurrency protection is a typed payload member of the kind that needs it, so the accepting Station evaluates it against committed typed state rather than against a caller-authored predicate.
The Event carries no caller-selected commit base. Every Commit takes its predecessor from the accepting Station's own stream head.

The Event envelope carries no expected_revision. The field is a typed payload member of the kinds that define it (see event-payload.schema.json and realm_bootstrap_registry.ordinary_collaboration.ordered_slots[].expected_revision); at envelope level it would be a caller-authored admission predicate.
The Event carries no requirements block. Admission requirements are registered per Event kind and evaluated by the accepting Station.
The Event carries no unsigned sidecar block: every envelope member is inside the producer signature. 'unsigned' remains legal on recipient-scoped DeviceMessage delivery objects, which are not Events.

Renamed survivor of the removed producer-side authorization context. The Event envelope is closed and carries no caller-authored authorization state; the accepting governance Station resolves current authorization and policy from committed typed state inside the admission transaction.
